item.title: Biosecurity at the frontier
item.description: LatchBio's independent BioSecBench-Refusal evaluation found Grok 4.6 was the only model tested to score above 50% on both refusing disguised biohazards and completing routine biological work. (via xAI)

item.title: Setting Grok Bot loose on procurement
item.description: xAI gave Grok Bot access to vendor spend, contracts, and usage data; it surfaced more than $100,000 in direct savings. (via xAI)

item.title: Designing Grok Bot for a world of persistent agents
item.description: xAI published a design write-up on the Grok Bot avatar system and how the product was shaped around agents that keep running between conversations. (via xAI News)

item.title: Grok Bot for Enterprise
item.description: xAI made Grok Bot available to enterprises. Grok and Cursor Enterprise customers get two weeks of free usage and can invite their whole organization, including people without an existing seat. (via xAI News)

item.title: A 7-step operator's manual for multi-agent Grok Bot teams
item.description: A widely shared playbook (400K views) argues the single-bot era is over: build a Chief bot that routes and delegates, keep shared state in /workspace instead of chat, and gate every workflow with source, evidence, and action checks. Humans approve only money, publishing, and irreversible actions. (via AdiiX on X)

item.title: The Grok Bot PMs on persistent chats and building your first bot
item.description: Two SpaceXAI product managers who ship Grok Bot walked through their own bot teams in a 47-minute interview, with the headline claim that you should never be watching a context meter. A companion guide covers bots, skills, routines, plugins, and the shared cloud computer. (via Phosphen on X)

item.title: Musk: automatic token optimization is coming to Grok Bot
item.description: Elon Musk confirmed that automatic token optimization is coming to Grok Bot, part of a broader efficiency push across xAI. No percentages or pricing details yet, but the feature would cut usage costs for bot teams at the platform level. (via Elon Musk on X)

item.title: Grok Bot vs Grok Automations vs Grok Build: the builder's map
item.description: A comparison of xAI's three builder surfaces: autonomous bots, scheduled automations, and the free low-code Grok Build tool. (via Kingy AI)

item.title: Grok Bot now works with X
item.description: Bots can now plug into X directly, reading posts and acting inside the platform where most of the ecosystem's builders already live. Paid Grok Bot users get free X API credits to start, plus an X plugin for search, timelines, and bookmarks. (via xAI)

item.title: Grok Bot is now included with more plans
item.description: Grok Bot expanded beyond the top tiers to all SuperGrok, Cursor Pro, and Cursor Teams plans. Bot usage is separate from Grok and Cursor allowances, so delegated work no longer eats a subscriber's main quota. (via xAI)

item.title: Grok 4.6 lands on Microsoft Foundry
item.description: xAI's newest model becomes available through Microsoft's enterprise AI platform, a notable distribution step beyond Grok's own apps. (via xAI)

item.title: Grok Bot breaks down: how it differs from the Grok you know
item.description: A technical breakdown clarifying that Grok Bot is a separate product from the consumer chatbot on grok.com and X, and from the xAI API. (via Vellum)

item.title: Grok 4.6 on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
item.description: Grok 4.6 became available on Google's enterprise agent platform, giving teams that standardize on Vertex AI a path to xAI's latest model. (via xAI)

item.title: Persistent digital coworkers: Grok Bot's $120/month play
item.description: Coverage of Grok Bot's positioning as always-on agents that operate your apps, with the pricing that comes with it. (via VentureBeat)

item.title: Grok Bot enters beta as always-on AI teammates
item.description: The launch write-up: bots with their own computer that sign into the tools you already use and carry out multi-step work on their own. (via The Verge)
